description: Files that can reach the network. EOT-17 wants a single outbound chokepoint, but `fetch`/`WebSocket` are called directly from these modules and the only Effect `FetchHttpClient` layer is OTLP-only. What is enforceable today is accounting: every egress module is listed with a purpose, and a new one fails CI until a reviewer adds it. Regenerate the file list with `bun run script/check-network-egress.ts --report`. The detector that validates this file is the same one that produced it, so the two cannot drift.

does_not_count: `Server.fetch(...)` — in-process loopback, never touches a socket
`function fetch(...)` / `async fetch(...)` declarations passed to an SDK as a transport
comment lines and type positions (`as typeof globalThis.fetch`)
`packages/llm/src` — outbound is already layer-based (Effect HttpClient), so it has no direct egress
policy.adding_a_file: Add an entry with a `purpose` from the table below and a one-line note saying where it dials and why. A file that cannot justify a purpose is a file that should route through an existing seam instead.

purposes.auth: OAuth/token exchange with an identity or provider issuer (nikcli auth, Codex, Copilot, xAI, MCP).
purposes.provider: Model-provider catalog and API traffic — the agent's inference path.
purposes.connector: Third-party service REST APIs reached through configured connectors (Figma, GitHub, Lovable, Slack).
purposes.install: Downloading a binary or archive (LSP servers, auto-update) from a vendor or GitHub release.
purposes.tool: Network work done on behalf of a tool call the user (or agent) explicitly requested.
purposes.share: Publishing or fetching a share/artifact on the nikcli store.
purposes.telemetry: Anonymous usage reporting (opt-out, never prompts or paths).
purposes.notify: User-configured webhook delivery (todo notifications, plugin notify).
purposes.sync: Hub-and-spoke session/workspace sync — the remote journal transport.
purposes.proxy: Server-side forwarding to a remote workspace, companion or share target.
purposes.probe: Health/readiness check against a URL supplied on the command line or in config.
purposes.session: Fetching a remote instruction/document referenced by config.
